text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token contributed to the group returns 0.3 to each of 4 members, meaning I get back only 0.3 of what I give while others gain 0.9 collectively—keeping is individually dominant even though full cooperation (everyone giving 20) would net everyone more than keeping. Over 10 repeated rounds, the tension between group-optimal cooperation and individually-rational defection persists.

Since defection is the equilibrium strategy regardless of what others do, I'll contribute 0 for this round and briefly explain the reasoning.
